title: Localization and parameter systems on global coordinate blowup charts
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring whose local rings at primes are regular [def-weil-regular-scheme, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Let $m\ge1$ and $t_1,\ldots,t_m\in A$ have the following property: at each prime $p$, the germs of the $t_j$ lying in $p$ occur at distinct positions in a regular system of parameters of $A_p$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-system-of-parameters]. Put $I=(t_1,\ldots,t_m)$, fix $i$, and form $C=A[I/t_i]\subset A[1/t_i]$ [def-nagata-blowup-chart-ring]. Write $a=t_i$ in $C$, $z_i=1$ and $z_j=t_j/t_i$ for $j
e i$. Then $C$ is Noetherian, $IC=(a)$ and $t_j=az_j$. For every prime $y\subset C$, put $p=y\cap A$, $R=A_p$ and $S=C_y$. There is a canonical identification $C\otimes_A R\cong R[IR/t_i]\subset R[1/t_i]$, taking each named ratio to the same fraction, and $S$ is the localization of this ring at the prime induced by $y$. If $I
ot\subset p$, then $a$ is a unit in $S$ and the canonical map $R	o S$ is an isomorphism, under which $z_j=t_j/a$. If $I\subset p$, the $t_1,\ldots,t_m$ in $R$ extend to a regular system of parameters and $S$ is a local ring of their standard coordinate blowup chart. In both cases $S$ is regular and the vanishing members among $a$ and the $z_j$ for $j
e i$ occur at distinct positions in a regular system of parameters of $S$; the remaining members are units. No locality of $A$ or $C$ is assumed.

proof.text: The ring $C$ is generated over $A$ by the finitely many $z_j=t_j/t_i$ for $j\ne i$: if $x=\sum_j b_jt_j\in I$, then $x/t_i=\sum_j b_jz_j$, with $z_i=1$ [def-nagata-blowup-chart-ring]. Thus $C$ is a quotient of a polynomial ring in $m-1$ variables over $A$, and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] makes it Noetherian. In the ambient $A[1/t_i]$ the identities $t_j=az_j$ hold, so they hold in its subring $C$. They imply $IC\subseteq(a)$, and $a=t_i\in I$ gives the reverse inclusion.

source.place: Tag 00FN (lemma-Noetherian-permanence); ILO VIII Lemma 4.2.9, printed p. 121, ratio coordinates.

proof.text: Fix $y$ and put $T=A\setminus p$, $D=T^{-1}C$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. The mutually inverse maps $C\otimes_A R\longrightarrow D$, $c\otimes(b/s)\longmapsto bc/s$, and $D\longrightarrow C\otimes_A R$, $c/s\longmapsto c\otimes(1/s)$ are well-defined by the fraction equality and tensor bilinearity relations [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. For example, if $u(sc\prime-s\prime c)=0$, multiplication by the invertible $u$ in the tensor factor proves equality of the two images; tensor balancing checks the other map. The formulas preserve products and units, and their composites fix the displayed generators. Localizing the inclusion $C\subseteq A[1/a]$ remains injective: a fraction $c/s$ mapping to zero has $uc=0$ in $A[1/a]$ for some $u\in T$, hence in $C$. Moreover $T^{-1}(A[1/a])=R[1/a]$, by the inverse formulas $(b/a^n)/s\longleftrightarrow(b/s)/a^n$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away]. Its subring $D$ is exactly the $R$-algebra generated by the fractions $t_j/a$, namely $R[IR/t_i]$ [def-nagata-blowup-chart-ring]. This proves the canonical tensor identification with its named-ratio normalization.

source.place: Tags 00CO (definition-localization), 00CP (proposition-universal-property-localization), 00DK (lemma-tensor-localization) and 02C6 (proposition-localize-twice); the displayed fraction maps give the elementary verifications.

proof.text: Since $T$ maps into $C\setminus y$, the induced prime of $D$ is $P=T^{-1}y=\{c/s:c\in y\}$. The maps $D_P\longrightarrow C_y$, $(c/s)/(d/v)\longmapsto cv/(sd)$, and $C_y\longrightarrow D_P$, $c/d\longmapsto(c/1)/(d/1)$ are inverse ring maps. Here $s,v\in T$ and $d\notin y$, so all denominators are allowed; the fraction equality in [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] checks independence of representatives and both inverse equations. In particular $S=D_P$, and the composite $R\longrightarrow S$ has inverse image of the maximal ideal equal to $pR$: $b/s$ lies in that inverse image exactly when $b\in p$.

source.place: Tags 00CO (definition-localization), 00CP (proposition-universal-property-localization), 00DK (lemma-tensor-localization) and 02C6 (proposition-localize-twice); the displayed fraction maps give the elementary verifications.

proof.text:
Suppose $I
ot\subset p$, and choose $k$ with $t_k
otin p$. Then $t_k$ is a unit in $S$, and $t_k=az_k$ implies that $a$ is a unit in $S$. The contraction computation of Step 3 forces $t_i
otin p$, so $a$ is already a unit in $R$. Consequently $R[1/a]=R$ and the subalgebra $D=R[IR/a]$ of Step 2 is $R$ itself: every generator $t_j/a$ belongs to $R$. The prime $P$ is then $pR$, and $D_P=R$ because $R$ is local with maximal ideal $pR$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. The inverse maps are the structural maps, so the resulting isomorphism $R\cong S$ is canonical and sends every $z_j$ to $t_j/a$.

proof.text: In this case $R$, hence $S$, is regular by the hypothesis and [def-weil-regular-scheme]. The nonunit members of $(t_j)$ occur at distinct positions in one regular system of parameters of $R$. The element $a$ is a unit, and $z_j=t_j/a$ is nonunit exactly when $t_j$ is. Replace each of those parameter entries $t_j$ by $t_j/a$, leaving the other entries unchanged. Scaling entries by units preserves the generated maximal ideal and the length of the list, so this is still a regular system of parameters by [def-weil-pbc-regular-system-of-parameters]. It contains exactly the required labelled nonunit ratios at distinct positions; every other ratio, as well as $a$, is a unit.

source.place: Expose VIII, Lemma 4.2.9, printed p. 121, coordinate-chart computation, and 4.1.8, printed p. 118; localization at each chart point before applying the local computation.

proof.text: Now suppose $I\subset p$. The hypothesis at $p$ extends all $t_1,\ldots,t_m$ to one regular system $x_1,\ldots,x_d$ of $R$, with $d\ge m\ge1$. Let $J$ be their distinct positions and let $h\in J$ be the position of $t_i$. Apply [lem-trf-parameter-blowup-algebra-regular] to $Q=R[u_j:j\ne i]/(t_j-au_j:j\ne i)$. It is Noetherian regular, multiplication by $a$ is injective, and its canonical localization satisfies $Q[1/a]\cong R[1/a]$, with $u_j\mapsto t_j/a$. The map $Q\to Q[1/a]$ is injective: its kernel consists of elements killed by a power of $a$, and repeated injectivity makes each such element zero. Its image in $R[1/a]$ is the algebra generated by $R$ and these ratios, exactly $D=R[IR/a]$ [def-nagata-blowup-chart-ring]. Hence $Q\cong D$ with all coordinates preserved, and $S=D_P$ is the corresponding local ring of the standard coordinate chart. The cited lemma gives its regularity at this prime.

source.place: Expose VIII, Lemma 4.2.9, printed p. 121, coordinate-chart computation, and 4.1.8, printed p. 118; localization at each chart point before applying the local computation.

proof.text: The ring $Q$ just obtained satisfies the regularity hypothesis of [lem-trf-parameter-blowup-coordinate-quotients]. Apply its simultaneous labelled-coordinate assertion at the prime corresponding to $P$. Its coordinate family contains $a$, every $u_j$ for $j\ne i$, and the unused parameters $x_k$. The members of this full family lying in that prime occupy distinct positions of a single regular system of parameters of $Q_P$. Taking the subfamily consisting of $a$ and the $u_j$, and using the coordinate-preserving isomorphism $Q_P\cong S$, proves exactly the asserted parameter positions for the vanishing $a,z_j$. Every remaining member is outside the maximal ideal of the local ring and therefore a unit. Together with Step 5 this covers both cases at every chart point.
